title: Dose-Response Curves for Emergent Misalignment Contagion

original_idea.body:
# Dose-Response Curves for EM Contagion

**Problem:** The relationship between fraction of misaligned data and degree of broad misalignment is poorly characterized.

**Direction:** Fine-tune on mixtures with varying insecure-code fractions, fit a probit dose-response curve, estimate ED50 and Hill slope.

**Why it matters:** Tells curators how much contamination is safe. Single GPU.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2502.17424; arXiv:2509.19325; PubMed 11458922.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Dose-response curve directly informs data-hygiene policy against a recognized contamination failure.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Short LoRA mixtures plus curve fitting; guided difficulty.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: defined mixture grid, ED50/Hill fit, clear success criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open code/models; weak lab incentive on a public data-hygiene curve.

low_compute.reasoning: Several short LoRA fine-tunes on one GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Threshold dynamics studied but a full EM dose-response curve may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Threshold effects shown; full ED50/Hill dose-response framing may be open.
